paper_title: Text Generation with Diffusion Language Models A Pre-training Approach   with Continuous Paragraph Denoise
caption: Effect of different diffusion steps on text generation quality, on XSum. The result is the optimal value of 5 Gaussian samples.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates how text generation quality on the XSum dataset varies across different diffusion step settings, reporting three ROUGE metrics for each setting (noted in the caption as using an optimal value of 5 Gaussian samples). The horizontal axis contains the categorical diffusion-step settings labeled “Diffusion Step,” shown in ascending order as 100, 250, 500, 1000, and 2000. The vertical axis represents ROUGE score values on a linear numeric scale (axis label and tick labels are not visibly provided), with bar-top annotations indicating values spanning roughly from near 0 up to about 41.2. For each diffusion step, three adjacent (grouped) bars are shown: ROUGE-1 is a blue diagonally hatched bar, ROUGE-2 is a light green dotted/hatched bar, and ROUGE-L is an orange crosshatched bar, as indicated by the legend in the upper-left of the plot area. At diffusion step 100, the bars are labeled 6.3 (ROUGE-1), 0.1 (ROUGE-2), and 3.0 (ROUGE-L); at 250 they are 11.6, 0.4, and 8.3; at 500 they are 21.1, 4.1, and 15.9; at 1000 they are 38.3, 16.5, and 30.7; and at 2000 they are 41.2, 19.1, and 33.4. The bars are grouped by diffusion step with consistent left-to-right ordering within each group (ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-L), and no bars appear specially emphasized beyond the distinct colors/patterns and numeric value labels above each bar.
